prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's contrastive loss already down-weights non-critical edges (via `_edge_timing_weights`), but the *area-balance repair* (`_refine_partition_by_area`) still moves whichever macro most cheaply fixes area, ignoring timing — so it can rip a timing-critical macro across tiers. Penalize moves of timing-critical macros (high incident critical-edge weight) by requiring larger area improvement before accepting them, so balance repair preserves critical-path locality.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:KeyError in partition; bp_fe-ng45/1003:legalization overlap; bp-ng45/1001:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1002:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1003:KeyError in partition
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed legality (overlap, HBT spacing), crash (KeyError in partition), and timeout failures across all seeds of both cases — systematic, not sporadic. This candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. The KeyError and timeouts suggest the added criticality-weight logic breaks partition bookkeeping or explodes runtime; overlaps/spacing suggest repair no longer converges. To make the idea legal: gate the penalty behind a bounded weight, guard missing edge-weight keys, cap repair iterations, and re-run legality checks after each accepted move.
